findings.evidence: features/003-complete-skill/003-complete-skill-prd.md:R3 + AC-3 — R3 says '`escaped_issues` — count + brief description of issues found AFTER ship (production incident, code-review catch, follow-up bug). At retro time the default for `escaped_issues` is `{count: 0, descriptions: []}`; the field is amendable later via `--amend --escaped-issue` (R10).' AC-3 enforces a non-null default at retro time: 'At retro time the default for `escaped_issues` is `{count: 0, descriptions: [], blast_radii: []}`.' But the PRD does not articulate the load-bearing assumption that escaped issues are typically *not knowable* at retro time — they surface days or weeks after ship. The default-0-at-retro-time framing implies the retro is the primary capture surface for escaped issues, when in fact the AMEND path (R10) is the primary capture surface and the retro-time default is a placeholder. The user's interview Round 2 edit explicitly named this: 'escaped_issues should be capturable both at completion (count: 0 known so far) AND amendable later when one is found ... Treating escaped issues as fixed at retro time loses the post-ship signal `/insights` reads later.' The PRD captures the amend path (R10) but doesn't name the assumption that retro-time `escaped_issues` is almost always 0 by definition, with the real signal arriving via amend. Without this articulated, a future reader (or a downstream `/insights`-cadence skill) may infer that retro-time escaped_issues = 0 means 'no escaped issues' rather than 'no escaped issues YET'.
findings.claim: Missing tradeoff articulation + unstated load-bearing assumption — R3 + AC-3's `escaped_issues` field defaults to `count: 0` at retro time without naming the load-bearing assumption that escaped issues surface post-retro and that the AMEND path (R10) is the primary capture surface. Think Before Coding principle: 'Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs. State assumptions explicitly.' The assumption is hidden in the PRD's prose but not articulated as a contract. Downstream consumers (`/insights`, similarity-search) reading the corpus will not be able to distinguish 'escaped_issues = 0 at retro time' from 'escaped_issues = 0 confirmed post-ship' without an additional field naming the capture state. The corpus loses signal: a task with no escaped issues looks identical to a task whose escaped issues haven't surfaced yet.
findings.proposed_change: Add an explicit `escaped_issues_capture_state` field to the schema (or rename `escaped_issues.count: 0` to a tri-state enum). Two options: (a) add `escaped_issues.capture_state: 'retro-time-default | amended-zero-confirmed | amended-with-issues'` so the corpus can distinguish 'no-issues-known-yet' from 'no-issues-after-six-months-confirmed' from 'issues-amended'; OR (b) extend R3 + AC-3 to articulate the load-bearing assumption as a Note in the PRD body: 'At retro time, `escaped_issues.count: 0` is the canonical default — escaped issues by definition surface post-retro, so any non-zero retro-time value is anomalous (e.g. issue found in code review between Verifier-pass and PR-merge). The AMEND path (R10) is the primary capture surface for escaped issues; consumers reading the corpus should treat retro-time `escaped_issues = 0` as 'unknown' until the entry has an `addenda` array entry confirming zero, not as 'confirmed zero.'' Option (a) makes the assumption mechanically observable; option (b) makes it documentation-only. Either resolves the unstated assumption.

findings.evidence: features/003-complete-skill/003-complete-skill-prd.md:R4 + AC-4 — R4 + AC-4 specify that the retro write supersedes Phase F's `what_worked`, `what_didnt_work`, `ai_assistance_level` values 'in place' on the existing entry. The PRD's Schema Appendix shows `superseded_by_retro: true` as the lineage flag. But the supersede is described as 'replaces those values in place' AND the schema appendix shows the entry has only one set of fields (the post-supersede values). The original Phase F values are NOT preserved anywhere — once superseded, the placeholder values are lost. For the `/insights`-cadence pattern detection that the goal's Driving value names ('decisions inconsistent failure mode' surfaced via lessons evaporating), the divergence between the Phase F initial guess and the user's retro-time reflection IS itself a learnable signal — e.g. tasks where the Phase F write said `ai_assistance_level: full` but the retro write says `partial` are tasks where the implementation surface was less AI-led than the orchestration thought. Discarding the Phase F values destroys that signal.
findings.claim: Single-interpretation framing of a tradeoff that has two viable approaches — R4 's 'replaces in place' framing eliminates the alternative of preserving both values (Phase F initial + retro reflection) for `/insights`-cadence divergence detection, without articulating why the elimination happened. Think Before Coding principle: 'Present multiple interpretations when ambiguity exists. Push back when a simpler approach exists.' The simpler approach (replace-in-place) was chosen without naming the cost (loss of Phase-F-vs-retro divergence signal); the alternative (preserve both) was eliminated silently.
findings.proposed_change: Edit R4 to articulate the tradeoff explicitly: 'The supersede is a write-in-place on the existing entry; the original Phase F values are NOT preserved. Tradeoff: this loses the Phase-F-vs-retro divergence signal (e.g. tasks where Phase F said `full` and retro says `partial` are a learnable pattern). Decision: the v1 schema discards the Phase F values to keep the entry shape simple (one source of truth per field, lineage observable via `superseded_by_retro` flag). v2 may preserve Phase F values as `phase_f_*` mirror fields if `/insights`-cadence pattern detection surfaces a real divergence-signal consumer.' This makes the tradeoff visible and the elimination defensible. No schema change in v1 — just the rationale.
